title: Moment
description: A GoPro lies on the grass looking straight up into a summer sky, and a man jumps over it. Two frames, half a second apart, are all there is: drag across the picture and you move through the instant between them, his arms opening and his feet coming at you along their real motion, while the camera drifts a few degrees round him so the tree, the post and the hotel slide against the cumulus. Nothing between the two presses was filmed; it is rebuilt from depth, layers and flow.
intent: 3D Moments (Wang et al., CVPR 2022, https://3d-moments.github.io/ , Apache-2.0): space-time view synthesis from two near-duplicate photos, done DIY on CPU after factory/reality/techniques.md section 11 and herb's depth research (factory/reality/crowdvolt-depth-heroes.md). Clean plate from the clip's own frames (LaMa only for the last 0.25 %), sky deepened toward the zenith, sky/near layers with MoGe-2 depth (the post and its wires a layer of their own on one rigid plane, and near-layer triangles that span a depth step over open sky collapsed, so a disocclusion shows the sky layer rather than a rubber sheet), SAM 2.1 mattes, DIS flow chained through the frames between the two presses, bidirectional mesh warp in the shader, shared film grade (summer). ?t=0..1 time, ?cam=-1..1 orbit.

sources.note: 1920x1440, 24 fps, 6.5 s, GoPro on the ground. Frames 78 and 90 are the two shutter presses that ship; frames 0-120 were used only to clear the plate behind the jumper (YOLO boxes say which frames may lend a pixel) and to track his motion (DIS flow chained frame to frame). Registered by phase correlation (about 2 px of drift); the hotel's name on its canopy (LaMa) and the birds (Telea) removed; the sky layer re-baked from frames 0-112 at full resolution with no smoothing (registered on the drifting cloud; each pixel a trimmed temporal median of the nine usable frames nearest the shutter, the near-clipped cores from the single least-clipped frame round them), the cloud graded as its own pass (local contrast, a filmic shoulder that stops the warm tops near 245, a luminance-keyed split tone: sunlit tops to #F4EEE4, skylit undersides to #9FB6CF) and a dithered radial zenith gradient on the blue; the overhead wires' ghosts pushed out of it; the birch re-matted by closed-form matting on the frames (its leaf gaps open onto the sky layer instead of carrying painted sky; the three wires to the post traced as continuous lines; floaters under 200 px dropped); shown full-bleed: the plate cover-cropped to the viewport with the jumper on a thirds line, the camera rolled 5 degrees so the post, wires and hotel converge on diagonals. The jumper re-cut from the clip's native 1920x1440 frames (708x732 sprites, never resampled; the matte's edge re-solved by closed-form matting at that scale, edge colour unmixed from the sky, motion packed at full sprite resolution) and graded as his own pass: shadow chroma smoothed, then a cool skylight fill (hue ~210) that wraps round what faces up, so the face, the arms and the soles read against the sky; no sharpening. The hotel re-matted against the sky last (closed-form matting on the facade-registered frames 78-90): its crown's lattice is open, every gap between the white ribs showing the sky layer, which carries the cloud the gaps saw in the sky pass's own grade, and its edge with the sky is cut hard and antialiased (about a plate pixel of ramp), pulled in 1.25 px, the colour unmixed against the sky behind it. Last, the post and its wires lifted out of the near layer into their own (post.webp): the strips of sky its matte had carried (cloud between the overhead wires, blue between the shaft and its cables, the sky inside the crossarm) dropped, the three cables down the shaft traced as straight lines, every wire one dark neutral, the whole rig warped on one plane of disparity fitted to the shaft; under it the sky layer's pale column and the wires' ghosts filled from the open sky beside them. The sky layer then rebuilt at twice the plate (3200x2132): the cloud's drawing re-merged from the clip's native 1920x1440 frames (a trimmed mean of the 17 clear frames nearest the shutter, registered on the cloud, so the H.264 blocks average out), with no edge-preserving deblock (the luminance left as merged, the chroma softened by a 1.5 px gaussian), lifted to output resolution with Lanczos and no sharpening; the blue takes the plate sky's grade, transferred at the scale of the form, and the cloud is regraded from the merge by global curves only (a filmic shoulder that rolls the clipped cores off near 236, a broad glow into the heart of each core, the billows opened a little, a split tone from sunlit #F4EEE4 tops to skylit #9FB6CF undersides), and a gentle warm diffusion bled from the sunlit tops into the blue round them; the fine texture on screen is the film's 24 fps grain. In the browser he is lit as if by a fill flash (about +1.5 stops in linear light on his matte alone, warmer than the skylight, his own colour kept inside his matte past the film's cool dye bleed), the shaded canopy's chroma deblocked and its blue spill taken out, its shadows opened on a power curve before the film, and the film's black lifted to a dense blue-teal toe (about 14/22/30) that keeps the leaves' drawing under the grain. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/moment/ (analyse, people, plate, flow, cleanup, export, matte, sky, jumper, crown, skyhr, post).
